name: Question 6
problem:
The displacement $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
r=⟨6{t}^{3/2},\,{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=4\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate $r$ to get the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{1/2},\,3{t}^{2}-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9{t}^{1/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{9}{2\sqrt{t}},\,6t-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot ⟨\frac{9}{2\sqrt{t}},\,6t-6⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{18}{\sqrt{t}},\,24t-24⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $t=4\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(4) & =⟨\frac{18}{\sqrt{4}},\,24(4)-24⟩ \\  & =⟨9,\,72⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the resultant force acting on $P$ when $t=4\,\text{s}$ equals $⟨9,\,72⟩\,\text{N}.$

Question 6
?

The displacement r, in meters, of a particle P of mass 4kg is given by r=⟨6t3/2,t3−3t2⟩, where t>0 is the time in seconds. Calculate the resultant force acting on the particle when t=4s.

a
 ⟨3,48⟩N
b
 ⟨9,24⟩N
c
 ⟨9,72⟩N
d
 ⟨3,72⟩N
e
 ⟨6,48⟩N
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Newton’s second law states that F=ma, where F is the resultant force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate r to get the velocity vector:

v=drdt=⟨ddt(6t3/2),ddt(t3−3t2)⟩=⟨9t1/2,3t2−6t⟩

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

a=dvdt=⟨ddt(9t1/2),ddt(3t2−6t)⟩=⟨92t,6t−6⟩

Therefore, the resultant force F at time t equals

F=ma=4⋅⟨92t,6t−6⟩=⟨18t,24t−24⟩.

Finally, when t=4s, we have

F(4)=⟨184,24(4)−24⟩=⟨9,72⟩.

Therefore, we conclude that the resultant force acting on P when t=4s equals ⟨9,72⟩N.
